title: Wilhelm cracks the ritual integration over the winter
notes: Wilhelm's winter work at Carrick: the folk system stops being spontaneous-only. He judges the formulaic-ritual step 'really easy — someone just needed to point it out'; the remaining work is formalizing the Artes Liberales / Philosophiae contribution.
source: Session recap 2026-07-25 (Ars Magica transcript), winter-1223 downtime.
body_text:
Wintering at **Carrick** while his research assistants are out gathering material, Wilhelm spends the season on **integration and research** — turning his folk system from a curiosity into something with proper mechanics.
**The breakthrough he's most confident about:** his current system knows only **spontaneous, ritual-style casting** (roll halved). Proper **formulaic** magic would let a caster add **Artes Liberales** and **Philosophiae** to the effort *and* drop the divide-by-two — roughly tripling the effective pool. Over the winter he works out that this ritual integration is, in his own estimate, **"really easy — someone just needed to point it out"**: give a caster the finished formula rather than making them improvise it each time.
**The Artes Liberales angle** is the part still taking his time: the obvious-once-said refinements a folk caster never bothered to name. If a ceremony wants a circle, it helps to know **geometry** enough to draw a true one; if it wants words of power, it helps to know **rhetoric** enough to project the voice. Formalizing how Artes Liberales and Philosophiae feed the working is the winter's real labor.
**Logistics.** His assistants are sent west and south to gather hedge-magic insight, carrying **sacks of grain and silver** as payment for anyone willing to teach the "easy stuff." Wilhelm writes letters — to the loose **wizard-circle** he keeps looped in on the project, to his family, and to **Dietrich** (his brother/scribe, back at his teaching post), whom he promises a **tractatus of the generated folk-magic spells** once it's finished. He intends to set up a **lab on shore** (he is chronically seasick and will not stay aboard ship an hour longer than he must), and has arranged for his research materials to be relocated from home toward wherever the covenant next bases itself. Feeds t019, t009, and the mundane vis-factory pitch (t020).

title: Wilhelm's capricorn: the Mill Pond goat named Joseph
notes: Surfaced when Éogan raised his capricorn hunt. Real capricorn lore for the saga; feeds t070 (Éogan's capricorn) and gives Wilhelm his own connection to the creatures.
source: Session recap 2026-09-19 (Ars Magica transcript) + owner notes.
body_text:
When Éogan speaks of the capricorn, Wilhelm puts up his glasses and shares a childhood memory: he and his brother **Patrick** used to play, month after month, with a **capricorn** — "Mr. Goat," whose name was **Joseph** — that appeared in the **Mill Pond** near their home on the **waxing moon**, three or four days at a time. A woman (likely a **dryad**) tended it; once, thinking the goat was drowning, the boys ran to save it, and she gently called them off — it was a **goat-fish**, not a goat. That wonder is why Wilhelm (and his brother) turned to magic.
What Wilhelm has since read: capricorns are **associated with water**; one is said to have relayed **God's warning to Noah** to build the ark before the flood; they are known to **teach survival** to people in dire need far from civilization; and they are **tricksters** — of humans and of much greater beings alike. Different regions produce different capricorns depending on the local fish; despite the name, they are **not truly goats**.

title: Wilhelm at Durenmar: books, Roots, and a stone sled (declared)
notes: Declared 1225 plan; expands the Durenmar trip. Costs settled by ruling. **Stone sled = 6 pawns Terram vis.** As a lesser enchanted device (single L20 effect) its cost is the instilling cost alone — 2 pawns, no opening step — so no Craft discount applies, and the Verditius sale price is a flat 3× = 6 pawns (ruling q033). The undiscounted-markup house rule in q033 only bites on greater/invested builds, not this one. **Roots = L6/Q24** (ruling q034). Both are covenant expenditures / acquisitions to log once the trip is played; specific Roots enter the library only when actually obtained. Not yet played.
source: Session recap 2026-09-19 (Ars Magica transcript) + owner notes.
body_text: Declared: Wilhelm means to raise **Artes Liberales** and **Philosophiae**, travel to **Durenmar** to acquire books, and **reconnect with his research assistants**. Among the books he hopes to source are one or more **Roots** — the standard foundational Art summae described in *Covenants* (p.93, Standard Texts), adopted by the saga as **L6 / Q24** and Redcap-deliverable “for a very small consideration” (ruling q034). He also asks to take **6 pawns of Terram vis** to purchase a **stone sled** from a Verditius crafter: a level-20 enchanted two-tonne stone slab that flies at ~45 mph and carries ~2,000 lbs — a way to move small groups (magi) “at the speed of plot” to distant plot sources, and for Wilhelm to visit his family more readily.

title: The Great Conjunction of Jupiter & Saturn (upcoming)
notes: Upcoming celestial event / campaign clock, not yet reached. Jupiter and Saturn close to ~2.1 arcminutes in Aquarius on the evening of 4–5 March 1226 — the closest observable great conjunction between 1226 and 2020. It makes the deepest (level-5) crossing of the Carnac Regio survivable for a single night: the lock is on the PATH, not the aura (Magic auras do not fluctuate cyclically). Anchored at Aldebaran (a Behenian fixed star); the Hyades are the classical rainy stars, matching the covenant's maritime regio grammar. Dagmar's premonitions + astrology make the date his to discover in character. (Placed in Spring 1226 by GM decision — filed after Winter — though the conjunction is technically 4–5 March.)
source: next_session_scenes.json → meta.campaign_clock ('The Great Conjunction of 4–5 March 1226').
body_text: On the evening of 4–5 March 1226, Jupiter and Saturn draw within ~2.1 arcminutes in Aquarius — the closest observable great conjunction between 1226 and 2020. For one night it makes the deepest (level-5) crossing of the Carnac Regio survivable.
